messages.subject: Combining different variables from differents subject in the same model
parts:
Hello :)

I'm wondering if I can combine different datasets with differents variables to answer the same question.

Let's say I have :
- one survey to measure Fatigue
- two surveys to measure Depression (DeprA and DeprB).
- two groups of subjects (Group1 and Group2)
- a Pre-Post design

My data looks like that :
 
                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               

My model is something like that :
Latent_Depr_PRE =~ DeprA_PRE +DeprB_PRE
Latent_Depr_POST =~ DeprA_POST +DeprB_POST

Fatigue_POST + Latent_Depr_POST ~ Fatigue_PRE + Latent_Depr_PRE

I want to combine these datasets to get more robust results, however, I'm sure I'm missing something to get the proper approach. When I run this kind of model, obviously, I get this warning : Due to missing values, some pairwise combinations have less than 10% coverage.

Do you have any ideas ?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Combining different variables from differents subject in the same model
parts:
You can fit models with different variables per group using the block-structure model syntax, like for multilevel models:

https://groups.google.com/g/lavaan/c/uyq3h0wXh6g/m/wne8Z83wAwAJ

With only a single indicator of depression in each group, you have to assume invariance, so you would just define different regression models per group:

mod <- '
group: 1
  Fatigue_POST + DeprA_POST ~ Fatigue_PRE + DeprA_PRE
group: 2
  Fatigue_POST + DeprB_POST ~ Fatigue_PRE + DeprB_PRE
'

You can label parameters to test equivalence across groups (assuming metric invariance).  If there is overlap in the items between the 2 surveys/scales, then you can define latent factors with different items per group, but still test measurement invariance for the overlapping items.
